label: Records of a store
description: What may be asked of the records a store keeps. Every operation names the store and the collection and nothing else: the collection declares the shape, so $T is the record's type and $K is its key's, both read from the store document rather than repeated here. None is pure -- each one reads or writes what outlives the run -- so each lives in a data graph and is listed in the feature's effects.

get.description: One record by its key. Answers record absent where the collection holds none under it, so a graph routes on has(record) rather than on a failure.

store.description: the path of the store document these records are kept by

collection.description: the collection of that store, by the name it declares

key.description: the value of the collection's key field

scope.description: The caller's scope over a scoped collection: an object with one key per column the collection's `scoped` declares, each the read the store binds for it. Written by the compiler from the store, never by a document. The engine writes these columns on `put` and holds every read, `patch` and `remove` to them, so a key of another scope is absent. Absent over a collection that declares no `scoped`, and over a view, which sees every row.

find.description: Every record the filter matches, in the order asked for. A find with no where answers the whole collection, which is what a small one is for; a large one is paged with limit and offset.

store.description: the path of the store document these records are kept by

collection.description: the collection of that store, by the name it declares

where.description: which records match. An object whose keys are fields of the collection's shape: a literal or a read ("{{in.method}}") means equality, and an object means a predicate, with one or more of eq, ne, lt, lte, gt, gte (the field's type), in, notIn (a list of it), has (boolean: present or absent, for an optional field), contains, startsWith (strings). Three combinators sit beside field names: all, any (lists of filters) and not (one filter). A field that is a shape or a list may only be tested with has. Nothing else is a filter. Absent: every record.

order.description: order by the first, then by the second where the first ties. Absent: the engine's own order, which is not promised to be stable

offset.description: skip this many first; it means nothing without an order

put.description: Write one whole record under its own key. The one verb that writes: with replace (the default) it is the upsert the name suggests, and with "replace": false it writes nothing where a record of that key exists and answers conflict, so a graph routes on that rather than on a failure. A constraint the store declares is answered the same way: a unique another record already holds, or a refs pointing at a record that is not there, answers violated and writes nothing. Nothing is filled in silently -- a new record's key comes from newKey.

record.description: the record as stored; absent where a conflict or a violated constraint stopped the write

conflict.description: a record of that key existed and replace was false, so nothing was written

violated.description: the constraint that stopped the write, named as the store declares it -- "unique [url, method]" or "refs notes.entryId -> entries". Absent where none did, so a graph routes on has(violated)

patch.description: Change some fields of one record, leaving the rest as they are. It never removes a field -- absence is written by put -- and it never touches the key. Answers record absent where the collection holds none under that key.

changes.description: an object whose keys are fields of the shape other than the key, each a value of that field's type

Absent over a collection that declares no `scoped`, and over a view, which sees every row.

remove.description: Remove one record by its key, and answer the record that was removed -- absent where the collection held none under it. A record another collection still references by a declared refs is kept rather than orphaned: removed is false and referencedBy names the reference, so a graph routes on that rather than on a failure.

record.description: the record as it was; absent where there was none, and still there where a reference kept it

removed.description: the record was there and is gone. False where the collection held none under that key, and where a reference kept it

referencedBy.description: the reference that kept the record, named as the store declares it -- "refs notes.entryId -> entries". Absent where none did, so a graph routes on has(referencedBy)

newKey.description: A fresh key no record of the collection has, of whatever type the collection's key field is. A graph asks for one before it puts a new record, so that what identifies a record is written by a node a reader can see.
